column1: # The ten-task cross-language corpus.  name <TAB> spec
# `{fn}` is substituted by batch.sh with the task name cased to the target
# language's convention -- see the README for why that is done here rather
# Every spec states its own edge cases.  An underspecified spec does not
# produce a harder task, it produces a test designer inventing an expectation:
# a live run wrote `assert word_count(' ') == 1` against a correct
# implementation, and the failure was about the spec rather than the model.

column2: a function {fn} that returns the sum of a list of integers; the empty list returns 0
a function {fn} that returns a string reversed; the empty string returns the empty string
a function {fn} that counts the vowels a e i o u in a string, counting both upper and lower case, and never counting y; the empty string returns 0
a function {fn} that returns the largest element of a list of integers; the list is guaranteed non-empty, so do not handle the empty case; a one-element list returns that element
a function {fn} that returns true when a string reads the same backwards; the comparison is exact, so case matters and spaces and punctuation count; the empty string is a palindrome
a function {fn} that returns the greatest common divisor of two non-negative integers; {fn} of x and 0 is x, and {fn} of 0 and 0 is 0
a function {fn} that returns a new list of integers with duplicates removed, keeping the FIRST occurrence of each value in its original order; the empty list returns an empty list
a function {fn} that returns a new list of integers sorted ascending, leaving the input list unchanged; duplicates are kept rather than collapsed; the empty list returns an empty list

a function {fn} that encodes a string of letters so that each run of one character becomes that character followed by the length of the run, including runs of length 1, so that "aaab" becomes "a3b1"; the empty string returns the empty string
a function {fn} that converts an integer between 1 and 3999 into its Roman numeral as a string, using the subtractive form, so that 4 is "IV", 9 is "IX" and 1994 is "MCMXCIV"
